source.title: Storyboard first, then let Claude edit (pause-and-play teardown)
source.creator: Chanyoung Ryu "Chandler" (@chandlerintelligence)
source.summary: Before Claude edits (or you shoot), have it write the whole video as a storyboard table of line, on-screen element, tool and sound cue, agree on it, then build. Shown as a pause-and-play breakdown of a $97 workflow with recipes for text behind the head, shadowed captions, a moody FFmpeg grade and a whip pan.

atoms.title: Storyboard table before any edit
atoms.text: Before Claude touches the footage (he does it even before shooting), it writes the whole video as a table: every line, what is on screen, which tool makes it. You fix the plan and agree on it, then Claude builds the edit from it. Chandler's columns: # / Freeze (time) / Chandler says / On screen.
atoms.how: Prompt: "Before editing anything, write the storyboard as a table: # | time | what I say | on screen | tool | sound cue. Wait for my OK." Review it, change rows, then say "build it".
atoms.quote: Before Claude edits anything, have it write a storyboard, so that you both agree on what the video looks like first. I always do this before I shoot.

atoms.title: SCORE and EMPHASIS lines per beat
atoms.text: The source creator's storyboard ("claude-editing / storyboard, v2, 24 beats") gives each beat timecodes, duration, shot type, the spoken line, a direction, an EMPHASIS line (which word goes gold serif, which is struck through) and a SCORE line with music cues such as "drop 1 on 'Claude did.'" and "tape stop under the scratch 0:28.3, drop 2 on 'storyboard'".
atoms.how: Add two fields to every storyboard row: EMPHASIS (word + treatment) and SCORE (music event + the exact word it lands on).

atoms.title: Half-second music dropout after the punchline
atoms.text: Right after the hook line "Claude did." the whole mix drops to near-silence (-42 LUFS) for about 0.5 s at 2.50 s, then the beat returns. The rest of the 85 s has no silence at all.
atoms.how: Cut the music (and room tone) for 0.4-0.6 s directly after the punchline word, then bring the beat back on the next line. CapCut: split the music and delete the 0.5 s piece.

atoms.title: Pause-and-play breakdown of a reel
atoms.text: Play another creator's popular or paid reel with its audio in a rounded card. Freeze it at each effect, shrink it to a thumbnail beside your head, explain how to make that effect, then play on. In L10 the source plays 10 times, 19.9 s of 85 s (23%), and its own lines carry the story.
atoms.how: Card top-right at ~50% width while it plays, ~13% width thumbnail while you talk; whoosh when it grows. Plan freeze times in the storyboard's Freeze column.

atoms.title: Undercut a paid course in the hook
atoms.text: Open with the rival's strongest line ("I didn't edit a single second of this video. Claude did."), then undercut its price: "This guy's selling this for 97 bucks. I'm giving it away for free." A $97 checkout card pops on the source as he says it.
atoms.quote: This guy's selling this for 97 bucks. I'm giving it away for free.

atoms.title: Text behind your head
atoms.text: Cut the speaker out with a person-segmentation model and put words on a layer between the background and the person, so the title sits behind the head. He uses it for the topic title, his brand name ("Chandler Intelligence", two-tone) and the CTA keyword "EDIT" (huge, outlined, low opacity).
atoms.how: AI: "cut me out with a person segmentation model, put the words behind me" (he renders with Remotion; HyperFrames can do the same). CapCut: duplicate the clip, Remove background on the top copy, put the text track between the two copies.
atoms.quote: Tell Claude to cut you out with a person's segmentation model, then put the words behind you using Remotion.

atoms.title: Demo each effect on your own shot
atoms.text: Each technique is applied to his own footage as he names it: grade-panel sliders move and his saturation measurably drops (SATAVG ~8 to ~4.5 at 56 s), his shot shrinks into the centre of the 3x3 wall, the words go behind his head. It works as proof and as a pattern interrupt.
atoms.how: In the storyboard, mark the word where each effect should switch on in your own shot, not just on the example.

atoms.title: Plain shadowed captions, no box
atoms.text: Captions as plain white bold sans (SF Pro/Inter-like) with a soft drop shadow and no background box, 1-3 words, centred at ~61% height just above the laptop edge. He calls it cleaner than the source's green box.
atoms.how: CapCut: Text > white bold sans, Shadow on (soft, ~40% opacity), no background; auto-captions split to 1-3 words.
atoms.quote: I'd lose the green box though. Plain text with shadow looks way cleaner.

atoms.title: Type the real prompt on screen
atoms.text: The exact prompt types on in a dark rounded chat bar with an orange send button (Claude-app look), top-centre above the head. Five full prompts are shown, so the viewer can screenshot them. Claude drew the bars as vector graphics.
atoms.how: Ask Claude: "draw a chat prompt bar as a vector graphic and type this text on, 1 character per frame".
atoms.quote: Ask Claude to draw these for you as vector graphics.

atoms.title: Real screenshot beats an AI mock-up
atoms.text: For UI graphics such as an editor timeline, a real screenshot looks better than a generated mock-up. He shows both, back to back.
atoms.how: Capture the real screen (timeline, app, settings) and put it in a rounded dark card; keep generated mock-ups for things that don't exist.
atoms.quote: You could create a mock-up of your editor timeline, but a real screenshot would look much better.

atoms.title: Tool card lands on the word
atoms.text: GitHub repo cards (openai/whisper, yt-dlp) and logo cards (FFmpeg) appear exactly when the tool is named, timed from Whisper word timestamps. The caption: captions, tool labels and repo cards "land exactly when I say them".
atoms.how: Get word timings (faster-whisper), then start each card on the first frame of its word, with a pop.
atoms.quote: Whisper gets the timing of every word, so captions, tool labels and GitHub repo cards land exactly when I say them.

atoms.title: Moody grade: highlights down, blacks up
atoms.text: His recommended look: curves pull the highlights down and lift the blacks, saturation down 15%, then a soft vignette. On-screen panel values: Highlights -35, Blacks +12, Saturation -15, Vignette -40. His own footage sits at mean luma ~25-28% with very low saturation and warm practical lamps.
atoms.how: CapCut/Edits Adjust: Highlights -35, Blacks +12, Saturation -15, Vignette -40. ffmpeg (our take): curves=all='0/0.05 0.75/0.66 1/0.88',eq=saturation=0.85,vignette=PI/5.
atoms.quote: Curves to pull the highlights down and lift the blacks. Saturation down 15%. Then a soft vignette.

atoms.title: Before/after slider reveals the grade
atoms.text: The source shows a warm look switched on, then a vertical slider wipes across to take it off: a before/after reveal. Chandler: FFmpeg makes the colour change, Remotion the slider.
atoms.how: Stack graded over ungraded and animate a vertical wipe mask with an eased move. CapCut: overlay the graded copy and keyframe a linear mask.
atoms.quote: FFMpeg for the color change and Remotion again for the slider effect.

atoms.title: Whip pan over recursive zoom
atoms.text: He skips the source's recursive zoom ("shrink the shot into a picture of itself, 3 levels deep, then push through it with a spin and blur") as "a bit too much" and uses a whip pan, which "looks cleaner". Measured: about 5 frames of horizontal motion blur into a new framing, with a whoosh and a hit.
atoms.how: Whip: 4-6 frames of directional blur/offset across the cut + whoosh starting ~2 frames before it. CapCut: Transitions > Swipe/Whip, ~0.2 s.
atoms.quote: For transitions I skipped the recursive zoom and went with a whip pan. It looks cleaner.

atoms.title: 3x3 wall of reels proves a trend
atoms.text: To show that "lots of people are doing this", his shot shrinks into the centre tile of a 3x3 grid and 8 downloaded reels pop in around it, one per frame. The grid then stays on as the thumbnail.
atoms.how: Download 8 examples with yt-dlp; prompt: "Shrink my shot into the centre tile of a 3x3 grid, then pop 8 of these reels in around it, one per frame."
atoms.quote: Shrink my shot into the centre tile of a 3x3 grid, then pop 8 of these reels in around it, one per frame.
